purpose: Atomic catalog of every mathematical formula used by the FSOT protein-structure pipeline. One entry per formula. Each formula will be stress-tested in isolation against measured observables before being put back into the assembled distogram. No free parameters — every coefficient must reduce to a closed form in {pi, e, phi, gamma}.

canonical_constants.S_BIOCHEM: domain_scalar('Biochemistry', D_eff=13, delta_psi=0.1, observed=false)  (FSOT-2.0 scalar engine output)

formulas.purpose: Collapse each of 20 amino acids to a balanced-ternary signature [Charge, Polarity, Volume] in {-1, 0, +1}^3. This is the bedrock — every downstream layer reads from this table.
formulas.derivation: Manual classification (Charge: acidic=-1, neutral=0, basic=+1; Polarity: nonpolar=-1, ambiguous=0, polar=+1; Volume: small=-1, medium=0, large=+1).
formulas.observable_target: Must correctly partition the 20 AAs along each axis vs canonical biochem tables (Kyte-Doolittle hydrophobicity, side-chain volume, side-chain pKa).
known_issues: G (Gly) currently [0,-1,-1] same as A (Ala) — but Gly has NO side chain and is uniquely flexible. Should it have its own row [0, 0, -1]?

I, L, M, F, W all collapse to [0,-1,+1] — five distinct AAs with same trinary signature. Acceptable at the trinary level, but every downstream chemistry term must distinguish them via the *scalar* mapping (F02), not the trinary.
H (His) charge = +1 but biologically charge is +0.5 at physiological pH. Trinary forces a choice; F02 stores 0.5 as the floating charge.
stress_tests_pending: Rank 20 AAs by hydrophobicity using ONLY trinary (polarity coord). Compare to Kyte-Doolittle. Expect Spearman > 0.8.
Re-derive Chargaff-pair complementarity: AAs of opposite charge should sum to zero in coord 0. Verify D+K, E+R sums are 0.

formulas.purpose: Map each AA to four continuous FSOT scalars: hydrophobicity_fsot, volume_fsot, charge, dipole_moment.
formulas.derivation:
Each scalar = closed form in {pi, e, phi, gamma}. Examples:
  G hydrophobicity = phi
  W hydrophobicity = phi^5
  K charge = +1, dipole = gamma*e^3
  D charge = -1, dipole = gamma*pi^3
formulas.observable_target: Hydrophobicity ordering vs Kyte-Doolittle; volume vs Zamyatnin side-chain volumes (cubic angstroms); charge vs net charge at pH 7; dipole vs measured dipole moments where available.
known_issues: Magic numbers 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 1.8, 2.0 appear in many rows (e.g. Y volume = pi^4 * 1.1, T volume = pi*e*1.4). These are FREE PARAMETERS in disguise. Must be replaced with closed forms in {pi, e, phi, gamma} or removed.

F (Phe) hydrophobicity = phi^4 ~= 6.85 but W (Trp) = phi^5 ~= 11.09 — Trp 60% more hydrophobic than Phe. Kyte-Doolittle has Phe 2.8, Trp -0.9 (Trp is actually LESS hydrophobic on the K-D scale because the indole ring H-bonds). Sign error here.
C (Cys) hydrophobicity = phi*1.2 ~= 1.94 — but Cys is moderately hydrophobic on K-D (+2.5). Currently sits below most aliphatics.
stress_tests_pending: Spearman rank of h column vs Kyte-Doolittle. Target >= 0.85.
Pearson of v column vs Zamyatnin volume. Target >= 0.95.
Eliminate all magic decimal numbers; rewrite each in {pi, e, phi, gamma}.

formulas.purpose: Strongest covalent interaction in the model — locks Cys-Cys pairs into closed loops, dominates crambin and many extracellular proteins.
formulas.current_form: fsot_chemical_interaction returns PHI.powi(6) when both AAs are Cys.
formulas.derivation: phi^6 ~= 17.94, chosen as 'largest force in the field'.
formulas.observable_target: Disulfide bond energy ~= 60 kcal/mol vs hydrophobic burial ~= 1-3 kcal/mol per residue. Ratio ~ 20:1 — phi^6 ~ 18:1 vs the typical hydrophobic term magnitude. Good match in magnitude.
known_issues: Fires on ANY Cys-Cys pair regardless of sequence separation. Real disulfides are bonded only when the two Cys side-chains are close in 3D — short loops (sep < ~5) are sterically forbidden; very long loops are entropically penalized. Should be gated by a sequence-separation envelope.
Doesn't distinguish reduced (free SH) from oxidized (S-S) Cys. In crambin all 6 Cys are disulfide-bonded; in many other proteins Cys are free.
stress_tests_pending: On 1CRN: top-3 predicted Cys-Cys pairs must match the 3 known disulfides (3-40, 4-32, 16-26).
Add sequence-separation envelope: ~ exp(-(s - s0)^2 / s0) where s0 = some closed form like pi*e.

formulas.purpose: Burial term — two hydrophobic residues attract in aqueous environment (water entropy gain); hydrophobic + hydrophilic repels.
formulas.current_form:
h_term = ((h1 - phi)/phi) * ((h2 - phi)/phi)
where h_i = hydrophobicity_fsot of residue i, phi acts as neutral threshold.
formulas.derivation: phi is the FSOT neutral pivot. Centering on phi and dividing by phi makes the term dimensionless and bidirectional: positive when both above OR both below threshold, negative when mixed.
formulas.observable_target: Should rank Ile-Leu, Val-Val, Phe-Phe pairs as strongly attractive (top decile). Should rank Lys-Asp as attractive only through F05 (charge), and Lys-Leu as weakly repulsive in aqueous.
known_issues: F02 has G hydrophobicity = phi exactly, so the term is 0 for any Gly pair — but Gly is technically hydrophobic on K-D. Probably correct as 'neutral pivot'.
Magnitude can exceed phi^6 (disulfide) for very hydrophobic pairs: W-W gives ((phi^5 - phi)/phi)^2 = (phi^4 - 1)^2 ~= 33.8. This is LARGER than disulfide. Wrong ordering.
No saturation — pair like W-W gets ~33.8 which dwarfs everything else and may explain why aromatic-heavy regions get bunched in the prediction.
stress_tests_pending: Compute pairwise h_term for all 400 AA pairs. Sort. Top-10 should be I-L, L-L, V-V, I-V, L-V, F-W, W-W, F-F, F-L, F-I. Verify.
Add saturation tanh(h_term/phi^3) or similar — but only if it remains zero-free-parameter.
Decide whether disulfide (F03) or hydrophobic (F04) should be the dominant scale. Currently F04 wins for W-W.

formulas.purpose: Coulomb-like: opposite charges attract, same charges repel.
formulas.current_form:
elec_term = -q1 * q2 * E
where q_i in {-1, -0.5, 0, +0.5, +1}.
formulas.derivation: Sign convention: -q1*q2 > 0 when charges opposite. Scaled by E (FSOT seed) ~= 2.718. Max magnitude e (K vs D or E).
formulas.observable_target: Salt-bridge energy ~ 3-5 kcal/mol in water (screened). Should be ~10x weaker than disulfide and ~comparable to a hydrogen bond.
known_issues: No distance dependence at all. Real Coulomb is 1/r. In our distogram the global envelope handles this, but the chemistry term itself is distance-blind.
His charge = 0.5 — fractional. Pairs like K-H give -0.5*e = -1.36 (attractive, half-strength). Reasonable.

No screening / Debye factor. In water at physiological ionic strength a salt bridge falls off as exp(-kappa*r) with kappa ~ 1/A. We can encode this in the envelope downstream but should consider here too.
stress_tests_pending: On 2GB1 (has lysine ladder K4, K10, K13 and acidic E15, E19, D22): top predicted electrostatic pairs should be K-E or K-D. Verify.
Compare ratio elec_term(K,D) / disulfide(C,C) = E / phi^6 ~= 2.72/17.94 ~= 0.151. Real ratio ~= 4kcal/60kcal ~= 0.067. We over-weight electrostatics by ~2.2x.

formulas.purpose: Weak attractive contribution from co-aligned polar moments.
formulas.current_form: dip_term = sqrt(mu1 * mu2) / (gamma * pi * e * e)
formulas.derivation: Geometric mean of both dipole moments, damped by gamma*pi*e^2 ~= 12.95 to keep below hydrophobic and disulfide forces.
formulas.observable_target: Dipole-dipole ~ 0.5-1 kcal/mol, weakest of the four. Should never dominate any pair.
known_issues: Always positive (attractive). Real dipole-dipole can be repulsive for anti-aligned moments. We have no orientation info, so always-attractive is a forced approximation.
sqrt of product loses sign — both dipoles always treated as same-sign.
F02 dipole values span gamma (=0.577) to gamma*e^4 (=31.5). sqrt(min*max)/12.95 = sqrt(0.577*31.5)/12.95 = 4.27/12.95 = 0.33. Magnitude reasonable.
stress_tests_pending: Verify magnitude never exceeds F04 or F05 for any pair.
Question: do we even need this term? Polar AAs already get charge=0 in F05 and intermediate hydrophobicity in F04. The dipole term may be redundant.

formulas.purpose: Flory random-walk baseline — residues close in sequence are close in 3D regardless of identity.
formulas.derivation: End-to-end distance of a random polymer of N segments scales as N^(1/2). Inverse gives proximity ~ 1/sqrt(sep).
formulas.observable_target: Cα-Cα distance vs sequence separation in unfolded peptides follows ~ sqrt(sep)*3.8 A. In folded proteins this dominates only for sep<6 because folding shortcuts long-range distances.
known_issues: Folded proteins are NOT random walks. The Flory law is for unstructured chains. In a folded protein the distance saturates around 30-40 A for any sep > ~30.
This term contributes 1.0 at sep=1, 0.71 at sep=2, 0.58 at sep=3. It dominates short-range and overwhelms the chemistry term unless gated.

No native FSOT derivation — Flory exponent 1/2 is a polymer-physics result, not FSOT. Can we get the 1/2 from {pi, e, phi, gamma}? Note 1/sqrt(2) is already in C_EFF and POOF. The exponent 1/2 itself is dimensionless.
stress_tests_pending: On a real folded protein, plot actual_dist[i,j] vs sep for all pairs. Fit 1/sqrt(sep) only for sep < 6. Quantify breakdown.
Try replacing with 1 / sep^eta_eff (eta_eff ~= 0.467). This is FSOT-native. Compare metrics.

formulas.purpose: Gate the chemistry term: short-range pairs are already covered by backbone, chemistry should peak at medium/long range where it adds information.
formulas.current_form:
env = s / (s + pi*e)
where s = sep, pi*e ~= 8.54.
formulas.derivation: Saturating envelope. env(s=1) = 1/9.54 = 0.105; env(s=8.54) = 0.5; env(s->inf) = 1.0. pi*e is the FSOT scale.
formulas.observable_target: Chemistry contribution should be near-zero for sep<3 (backbone bond geometry), rising through sep=6-12, plateauing at long range.
known_issues: Multiplies into chemistry — for very long sep (50+) chemistry is at full strength. But real protein contacts at sep > 30 are RARE (most residues that far apart never see each other in 3D). The envelope should saturate then DECAY, not plateau.
8.54 (pi*e) is a sensible turn-over scale (matches typical contact distance), but for a sequence separation the turn-over should probably be larger — maybe pi*e*phi ~= 13.8 or D_biochem = 13.
stress_tests_pending: On 1UBQ: plot mean chemistry contribution to actual contacts (true_dist < 8) vs non-contacts, binned by sep. Should be higher for contacts at all sep. Quantify.
Try envelope = (s/s0) * exp(-(s/s0_high)) — peaks then decays. s0 = pi*e, s0_high = D_biochem.

formulas.purpose: Set the absolute weight of the chemistry term relative to backbone, helix, sheet, region-pair layers.
formulas.derivation: S_molchem is the FSOT scalar for the Molecular_Chemistry domain (D_eff=9). P_NEW = (gamma/e)*sqrt(2) is the structural promotion constant.
formulas.observable_target: Chemistry should contribute ~30-50% of the long-range contact signal in a typical protein (vs ~30% backbone, ~20% SS).
known_issues: max(|S|, P_NEW) is a guard against S being near zero. Should we just use |S|? What does S_molchem actually equal numerically? Need to print and record.
Multiplying by P_NEW again may be double-counting (S already factors in some FSOT constants). Should be one or the other.
stress_tests_pending: Print S_BIOCHEM, S_MOLCHEM numerical values once, record in this JSON.
Ablation: set chem_amp = 1.0 (no scaling) — does Pearson change? If yes, the scaling matters; if no, it's cosmetic.

formulas.purpose: α-helix is a 3.6-residue-per-turn coil — residues at i, i+3, i+4, i+7 sit close in 3D. Boost predicted proximity for such pairs when both prefer α.
formulas.current_form:
if sep in {3, 4, 7}: bonus = (p_alpha_i * p_alpha_j)^1.5 / e
else 0
formulas.derivation: Geometric mean of α-propensities, cubed (powi(3) on sqrt = ^1.5), normalized by E.
formulas.observable_target: On 1ENH (3-α bundle, 54 AA): residues at i,i+3 and i,i+4 within each of the three helices should be top-ranked. Helices span roughly: H1 = res 8-19, H2 = res 27-39, H3 = res 41-52.
known_issues: Cube is empirical — no FSOT derivation for the exponent 3 here. Why not 2? Why not phi? Need closed-form justification or stress-test.
Treats sep=3, 4, 7 equally — but i,i+4 has Cα-Cα ~ 6.2 A while i,i+3 ~ 5.5 A and i,i+7 ~ 8 A. They should not all give the same bonus.
Fires even on isolated α-preferring residues that aren't actually in a helix. F12 regions layer mitigates this for the region-pair term but not for this local term.
stress_tests_pending: On 1VII (all-α): top-10 i,i+4 pairs should all be within the three helices. Count hits.
Add sep-specific weight: bonus *= phi/sqrt(sep), so sep=3 gets boost, sep=7 attenuated.
Gate by region membership: bonus only if both residues are in the SAME detected α region (zero free param — uses F12).

formulas.purpose: β-sheet pairs (parallel and antiparallel strands) bring residues from distant parts of the sequence into close 3D contact.
formulas.current_form:
if sep < 3: 0
else: bonus = (p_beta_i * p_beta_j) * 1 / (1 + ln(sep/pi).clamp(>=0)) / phi
formulas.derivation: Joint β-propensity squared, modulated by a heavy-tailed log envelope peaked at small sep, divided by phi.
formulas.observable_target: On 1UBQ: residues in β1 (2-7), β2 (10-17), β3 (40-45), β4 (48-49), β5 (64-72) should pair across strands. Five-stranded mixed sheet.
known_issues: Envelope decays MONOTONICALLY with sep — but ubiquitin β1-β5 are ~60 residues apart and DO pair (it's a five-stranded sheet). The current envelope at sep=60 = 1/(1+ln(60/3.14)) = 1/(1+2.95) = 0.253. Decent but the bonus is also multiplied by joint^2 which is small for non-extreme β residues.
Doesn't distinguish parallel from antiparallel pairs. They have different geometric registers.
No register concept (which residue on strand A pairs with which on strand B). Currently every β-β pair gets equal treatment.
stress_tests_pending: On 1UBQ: enumerate top-20 sheet_pair_bonus pairs. Should be β-β cross-strand. Count true contacts.
Compare antiparallel vs parallel β-pair positions in known sheets.

formulas.purpose: Collapse per-residue α/β/coil propensities into contiguous runs (≥3 residues) — the FSOT trinary triadic-collapse mechanism. Only collapsed regions can engage in cross-region long-range coupling.
formulas.current_form:
for each residue: collapse to H/E/C using gate p_dominant > 1/e AND p_dominant > the other.
A region = ≥3 consecutive residues of same kind.
formulas.derivation: 1/e ~= 0.368 is the FSOT uniform-prior threshold (1/3 + one nat of coherence above prior). Minimum length 3 = 3^1 = smallest trinary triad.
formulas.observable_target: Detected regions should approximately match DSSP-assigned secondary structure for each test protein.
known_issues: Gate of 1/e is arbitrary — phi/e (~0.595), 1/phi (~0.618), or 1 - 1/e (~0.632) might be better calibrated.

No-overlap rule: a residue can be in at most one region. But real proteins have helix-turn-helix motifs where the turn residues have intermediate propensity. We mark them coil, breaking the region — fine for our purpose.
Minimum length 3 — but α-helix needs 4+ residues for one turn, β-strand needs 3+. The 3 threshold lets in single-turn helices and short coil-like β. Could split: helix_min=4, strand_min=3.
stress_tests_pending: On each test protein: print detected regions side-by-side with DSSP. Compute Q3 accuracy (fraction of residues classified correctly).
Vary gate (1/e, 1/phi, 0.5) and minimum length. Pick the (gate, min_len) that maximizes Q3 across all 5 test proteins — but ONLY if those values come from {pi,e,phi,gamma}.

formulas.purpose: Long-range bonus for residue pairs that belong to two DIFFERENT same-kind collapsed regions (helix-helix packing or strand-strand pairing). The FSOT trinary higher-order coupling.
formulas.derivation: long_range_gate = ceil(eta_eff * 13) = 7. Logarithmic length factor because doubling region size shouldn't double the coupling. region_amp combines biochem-domain scalar with structural promotion.
formulas.observable_target: On 1ENH (3-α bundle): cross-helix residue pairs (H1-H2, H2-H3, H1-H3) should top the long-range contact list. On 2GB1: strand 1-2, 1-4, 3-4 pairings.
known_issues: NO ROTATIONAL REGISTER. Every residue in helix A couples equally to every residue in helix B. Real helix-helix packing is HEPTAD-registered: positions a,d (mod 7) face the partner. Missing this is why 1ENH long-range = 3.70%.

NO STRAND DIRECTION. Antiparallel β-pairs run in opposite directions: residue i on strand A pairs with residue (j_max - k) on strand B. Parallel pairs run same direction. Missing this is why 2GB1 long-range = 7.14%.

Length factor ln(sqrt(L_i*L_j)) — for L_i=L_j=3 this is ln(3) ~= 1.10. For L_i=L_j=20 it is ln(20) ~= 3.0. Roughly 3x stronger for big regions — but real coupling probably scales more like sqrt(min(L_i, L_j)) (the shorter region limits the interface).
region_amp uses S_biochem which we haven't actually printed/verified. May be large or small or even negative.
stress_tests_pending: Print numerical values: S_biochem, region_amp.
Add heptad register for helix-helix: residues at positions (start + k) where k mod 7 in {0, 3} get a phi multiplier, others get 1/phi.
Add strand register: enumerate antiparallel pairing (i on A <-> (end_B - (i - start_A)) on B) as the strong pairing, others suppressed.

formulas.purpose: Threshold above which sequence separation counts as 'long range' for the region-pair layer.
formulas.observable_target: Pairs with sep < gate are already covered by local layers (F10 helix or F11 sheet). Gate should be ~= the maximum within-region range for local layers — currently F10 max sep is 7, so gate=7 is consistent.
known_issues: Coincidentally 7 = max sep in F10's helical-period set {3,4,7}. Good — no overlap with local helix term. But for sheets F11 fires at all sep>=3, so there IS overlap with sheet term at sep 7+. Sheet term + region-pair term may double-count.
Closed-form value 6.07 rounded to 7 — could equally round to 6. Both come from FSOT seeds. Test sensitivity.
stress_tests_pending: Try gate = 6, 7, 8. Measure long-range precision on all 5 proteins. Pick the value that performs best AND has the cleanest closed form.

formulas.purpose: Final layered sum producing matrix[i][j] = predicted spatial proximity (larger = closer).
formulas.observable_target: Rank correlation with -1/actual_dist > 0.5 (Spearman). Top-L precision > 90%. Long-range precision: AlphaFold reports 70%+ on CASP14; we need to climb from ~10% to that asymptotically.
known_issues: Linear sum may not be the right combinator. Layers may be multiplicatively, not additively, related. Try matrix = backbone * (1 + chemistry + helix + sheet + region_pair).
No normalization. Layer magnitudes can vary by orders of magnitude — backbone ~1.0, chemistry ~0.1, helix ~0.06, sheet ~0.03, region_pair varies wildly with L_i, L_j.
Diagonal forced to 0 — but i=i is trivially proximity = infinity. Doesn't matter for benchmark (we skip diagonal).
Matrix is symmetric in formula but we fill both halves redundantly — 2x cost. Cosmetic.
stress_tests_pending: Per-protein, print mean magnitude of each layer for contacts vs non-contacts. Identify which layers actually discriminate.
Try multiplicative combine: matrix = backbone * exp(chemistry + helix + sheet + region_pair).
Try the FSOT scalar engine directly: matrix[i][j] = compute_scalar(params_for_pair(i,j)) where params encode the pair's chemistry+geometry.

missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.purpose: Helix-helix packing register — residues at positions 0,3 mod 7 face the partner helix in coiled-coils and bundles.
missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.evidence_from_data: 1ENH (3-α bundle) long-range precision = 3.70%. Without register every cross-helix pair gets the same bonus.
missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.fsot_motivation: 7 = 3+4 = the trinary triad sum, already appearing in F10 (helical periods {3,4,7}).
missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.proposed_form:
register_factor(k_i, k_j) = phi if (k_i mod 7 in {0,3} AND k_j mod 7 in {0,3}) else 1/phi.
Applied as a multiplier inside F13 for helix-helix pairs.

missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.purpose: β-strand pairing register — antiparallel vs parallel, with specific residue-to-residue correspondence.
missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.evidence_from_data: 2GB1 (α+β, has 4-strand β-sheet) long-range = 7.14%. Without strand register we're sampling random β-β pairs.
missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.fsot_motivation: Antiparallel = phase inversion (FSOT trinary spin flip). Parallel = same phase.
missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.proposed_form:
For two β regions A (start_A..end_A) and B (start_B..end_B):
  antiparallel pair: i in A <-> j_AP = end_B - (i - start_A).
  parallel pair:     i in A <-> j_P  = start_B + (i - start_A).
Bonus only for the register-matched pair index; off-register gets suppression 1/phi.

missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.purpose: Suppress disulfide for sequence separations that are sterically impossible (sep < 4) or entropically penalized (sep > 50).
missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.evidence_from_data: F03 fires on every Cys-Cys regardless of geometry. 1CRN disulfides are sep ~ 12-24; many proteins have NO disulfides despite having Cys.
missing_formulas_pointed_at_by_data.proposed_form: PHI^6 * gauss(sep; mu=pi*e*phi, sigma=pi*e) where mu ~ 13.8 (typical disulfide loop), sigma ~ 8.5.

test_protocol.description: Each formula is stress-tested in isolation before re-integration.
phases: 1. Print numerical values of all currently-uncomputed constants (S_BIOCHEM, S_MOLCHEM, P_NEW, chem_amp, region_amp).
2. For each formula F##, run its stress_tests_pending against the 5 benchmark proteins.
3. If formula passes its target, freeze it. If it fails, refine in {pi,e,phi,gamma} or replace.
4. After all formulas pass in isolation, re-assemble (F15) and re-run the 5-protein benchmark.
5. Expand benchmark set (β-barrel, αβα sandwich, larger proteins) and repeat.
non_negotiables: Every coefficient must be a closed form in {pi, e, phi, gamma}. No fitted decimals.
Long-range contact precision is the only metric that matters for 'meets or exceeds observable'. Top-L is dominated by backbone and is misleading.
Every formula change must be re-verified against ALL 5 proteins, not just the one it was designed for.
